claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and any children you're responsible for.

Let me start with a basic question:

**How many children are you responsible for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking into claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who is 4 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! That's helpful to know.

Now, to assess your eligibility, I need to understand your living situation:

**Do you live with Alex, or does Alex live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with me, but I should mention that their other parent also lives with us and already claims Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is an important detail.

I need to let you know that according to Child Benefit rules, **only one person can get Child Benefit for a child**. Since Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex, you would not be able to claim it as well.

If you believe you should be the one receiving Child Benefit instead, or if circumstances have changed, you would need to:

1. Contact the Child Benefit Office to explain the situation
2. Agree with the other parent about who should claim (if possible)
3. If you can't agree, HMRC will decide who gets it

However, let me ask: **Are there any other children you're responsible for that we haven't discussed yet?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex is my only child. So just to be clear - because my partner already claims Child Benefit for Alex, I'm not eligible to claim it myself, is that right?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's correct. Since only one person can get Child Benefit for each child, and your partner is already claiming it for Alex, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

However, if your circumstances change in the future—for example, if you and your partner agree that you should be the one claiming instead—you would be able to make a new claim at that time. You'd just need to contact the Child Benefit Office to make those arrangements.

Let me now provide you with a formal assessment of your eligibility:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary:** You are **not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex because your partner is already claiming for them. Only one person can claim Child Benefit per child.

If you have any other questions or if your situation changes, feel free to ask!
